overview: This map label covers eastern New Guinea and nearby islands long before a single state united them. Papua New Guinea became independent in 1975. Communities had their own languages, farming systems and exchange networks; later colonial administrations, warfare and nation-building changed their political relationships.

periods.title: Communities before colonial partition
periods.summary: The imported map begins before the German and British colonial territories were established.

periods.title: Colonial territories and self-government
periods.summary: Separate territories came under Australian administration; elected institutions and self-government preceded independence.

periods.title: Independent Papua New Guinea
periods.summary: Independence took effect on 16 September 1975, following self-government from December 1973.

items.text: Kuk’s buried cultivation mounds and drainage ditches preserve a much older history beneath today’s farmland. UNESCO dates clear agricultural change to roughly 7,000 to 6,400 years ago. These are ancient predecessors of the modern country, whose name should not be projected back onto a prehistoric state.

At Kuk, farmers propagated crops including bananas, taro and yams and later dug drainage channels with wooden tools. Managing wet ground helped make planting possible. The surviving landscape records repeated changes in practice rather than one invention that stayed exactly the same forever.

Motu-speaking communities carried pottery by large sailing canoes to Gulf communities in the hiri exchange, returning with sago and canoe hulls. The voyages connected households making cooking pots with households producing food. A useful kitchen vessel could travel far beyond its maker’s village.

An 1885 observation described hiri canoes carrying, on average, more than fifteen hundred pots each. Women’s pottery production and men’s canoe preparation required extensive coordination. Before the dramatic departure came a great deal of clay-working, building and packing.

Powerhouse preserves a finely looped bilum bag catalogued to 1960 to 2001. In his 2022 interpretation, Papua New Guinean scholar Michael Mel points to its fine continuous string, strengthened handles and carefully finished opening as signs of exceptional skill.

Mel explains how bark fibers were cured, teased into strands and rolled on the maker’s thigh to form string. He interprets the bag as a first-child carrier whose open loops allowed air through. Its exact regional attribution differs between the old catalog and his assessment.

Tok Pisin developed through contact among people speaking different languages, including workers brought together on Pacific plantations. Its history extends beyond New Guinea into wider labor networks. People created a shared means of communication under difficult and unequal conditions.

“Nau gavmen i tok” means “Now the Government is talking.” This Tok Pisin opening comes from an Australian Second World War leaflet reproduced and translated by linguist Peter Mühlhäusler. It is wartime persuasive writing in Latin letters, not an ancient traditional saying.

Germany annexed the northeast in 1884, while Britain established control in the southeast and formally annexed it in 1888. Australia assumed administration of Papua in 1906. These were imposed colonial jurisdictions across already inhabited lands, not empty spaces waiting for names.

Australian archives preserve correspondence on constitutional change alongside photographs of independence celebrations. The records trace the shift from an appointed legislative council to an elected House of Assembly in 1964. Written files and photographs document different parts of the same transition.

Michael Somare’s ministry, formed after the 1972 election, pursued self-government and independence. Self-government began on 1 December 1973, followed by independence on 16 September 1975. The present state’s beginning therefore lies centuries after the map’s imported 1715 starting point.

The constitution’s preamble honors inherited customs and connects individual dignity with community interdependence. It also favors consensus in resolving problems and places power in the people through elected representatives. The founding text brought several principles of national life together in writing.

ending.text: Colonial administration ended with independence in 1975, and Papua New Guinea continues as a state. Its many communities did not begin with independence. The imported 1715 date is geographical coverage, not the founding of a unified Papua New Guinean polity.
